Quick Answer

What are qPCR Virus Titer Kits?

abm’s qPCR Virus Titer Kits are ready-to-use viral vector quantification kits for measuring lentivirus, adeno-associated virus (AAV), and retrovirus titers by qPCR or RT-qPCR. They are designed for fast viral stock QC, MOI planning, and downstream experiment setup, with results in only 1 hour and no purification step needed.

What it does

Quantifies viral vectors by qPCR or RT-qPCR

Use the kits to measure viral titer for lentivirus, AAV, or retrovirus workflows so researchers can compare viral lots and plan downstream experiments with a measured input.

Which kit to choose

Match the kit to your viral system

  • LV900: qPCR Lentivirus Titer Kit for HIV-1-based lentivirus.
  • G931: qPCR AAV Titer Kit for AAV genome copy titration.
  • G949: qPCR Retrovirus Titer Kit for retroviral vector titration.

FAQ

qPCR Virus Titer Kit FAQs

Answers to common questions about using abm’s qPCR and RT-qPCR viral titer kits for lentivirus, AAV, and retrovirus workflows.

Which qPCR Virus Titer Kit should I use for lentivirus?
Use LV900, the qPCR Lentivirus Titer Kit, for HIV-1-based lentivirus titration by RT-qPCR. It is designed for supernatant or concentrated virus samples and supports MOI planning.
Which kit is designed for AAV titering?
Use G931, the qPCR AAV Titer Kit, for AAV genome copy titration. The kit supports AAV workflows with primers for CMV and ITR detection.
Which kit should I use for retrovirus titration?
Use G949, the qPCR Retrovirus Titer Kit, for retroviral vector titration by RT-qPCR. It supports retroviral stock QC and downstream workflow planning.
Do the qPCR Virus Titer Kits require sample purification?
No purification step is needed, helping reduce sample preparation and handling time before qPCR or RT-qPCR setup.
How quickly can the kits provide viral titer results?
The kits are designed to provide titer results in only 1 hour, supporting faster QC decisions and downstream experiment setup.
What are the main benefits of qPCR-based viral titering?
qPCR-based viral titering helps researchers measure viral input, compare viral lots, support viral stock QC, and plan downstream transduction experiments.
